courses.description: An introduction to major dance styles for musical theater including: fundamental performance skills, exercises in body awareness, and principles of choreography for musical theater pieces. Students address the process of creating a character through movement and develop audition and rehearsal techniques through in-class work and out-of-class assignments. This course includes a survey of the history of dance in musical theater.
courses.title: Musical Theatre Dance: Styles I

courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the basic technique and terminology of ballet. Through beginning-level barre and center work, students will explore kinesthetic and spatial awareness, alignment, musicality, and use of weight. Exercises in this course are designed to develop strength, balance, and flexibility. Students will practice professionalism and gain an appreciation and understanding of the art form.
courses.title: Ballet I: Classical Dance Technique

courses.description: A composition course focusing on skills required for effective writing in a variety of contexts, with emphasis on exposition, analysis, and argumentation, and also including introductory use of a variety of research skills.
courses.title: English Composition I

courses.description: A composition course that develops writing skills beyond the levels of proficiency required by ENGL 1101, that emphasizes interpretation, and evaluation, and that incorporates a variety of more advanced research methods.
courses.title: English Composition II

courses.description: Upper division study abroad course denoting junior, senior level work.
courses.title: Upper-division Study Abroad

courses.description: An introduction to theatre as a field of study and as an art form.
courses.title: Introduction to Theatre Studies

courses.description: This course introduces students to the skills required to make original performance work through collaboration.
courses.title: Devising Performance Lab

courses.description: An introduction to performance as a field of study and as an art form.
courses.title: Introduction to Performance Studies

courses.description: An overview of the theoretical and practical foundations of entertainment production, including core disciplines such as scenic carpentry, properties, costume construction, scene painting, stage lighting, and sound design. Students gain hands-on experience in theatre crafts while learning essential safety protocols and production workflows.
courses.title: Introduction to Technical Theatre

courses.description: The theory and practice of the actor’s craft.
courses.title: Acting I: Principles of Acting

courses.description: A study of the methods and materials used in the production of theatre scenery and lighting. Hands-on work in the scenic studio and theatres will be an important component of the course.
courses.title: Scenic and Lighting Production

courses.description: A study of the methods and materials used in the production of theatre costumes. Hands-on work in the costume studio and theatres will be an important component of the course.
courses.title: Costume Production

courses.description: A study of the creative process of theatrical show crew from concept to performance. Students will serve as a member of show crew for a production in the department season.
courses.title: Show Crew

courses.description: A foundational exploration of visual storytelling across entertainment. Students engage with core design principles, historical context, and current practices through lectures, analysis, and creative projects to build a versatile design vocabulary.
courses.title: Introduction to Entertainment Design

courses.description: The study of a variety of literary texts through solo and group performance. Students engage course topics through critical reading, written analysis, and embodied performance.
courses.title: Performing Literature

courses.description: This course focuses on basic skills in musical theatre singing styles and vocal health.
courses.title: Musical Theatre Techniques I

courses.description: This practical course focuses on the study, rehearsal, and methods of performance for a Department of Theatre and Performance Studies production for the student actor.
courses.title: Applied Performance and Production

courses.description: This practical course focuses on the pre-production process, rehearsals, and performances for a Department of Theatre and Performance Studies production for students focusing on design, stage management, or other production positions.
courses.title: Design and Production

courses.description: This practical course focuses on the pre-production process, rehearsals, and performances for a Department of Theatre and Performance Studies production for students focusing on creative team positions that include, but are not limited to: direction, writing, composition, choreography, or music direction.
courses.title: Production Creative Team

courses.description: This practical course focuses on the development of dramaturgy for a Department of Theatre and Performance Studies production. Students will engage in processes of pre-production, rehearsal, audience and community engagement, and the creation and dissemination of dramaturgy materials.
courses.title: Dramaturgy for Production

courses.description: The study of world mythology through storytelling performance.
courses.title: Performing World Myth

courses.description: The study of personal narratives through performance.
courses.title: Performing Personal Narrative

courses.description: This course is designed to help performers develop a healthy, expressive and flexible vocal technique equal to the demands of dramatic performance. Students learn to free their natural voices through physical exercises and by mastering the vocabulary of vocal mechanics. Breathing, posture, relaxation, and articulation are examined as key elements of voice and speech production.
courses.title: The Actor’s Voice

courses.description: This course introduces students to the anatomy, physiology and physicality of the actor’s voice and body. The approach is holistic mind, body and vocal practice. We explore what “physical freedom” and “embodied voice” mean, and how to use them both in performance. Techniques learned and practiced are applied directly to specific performance assignments.
courses.title: The Actor’s Instrument: Integrated Voice and Movement

courses.description: Movement for the Actor is a studio course dedicated to bringing awareness to the body as an essential part of the actor’s training. In this course, the student actor will explore the expressive capacity of the physical and emotional body in the context of acting.
courses.title: Movement for the Actor

courses.description: An intermediate acting course applying acting techniques to the special demands of film and television.
courses.title: Acting for the Camera

courses.description: An intermediate acting course applying and advancing the principles of Acting I to intermediate level stage challenges.
courses.title: Acting II: Intermediate Acting

courses.description: This course explores advanced topics in the art of stage acting. Emphasis is on period and genre styles. Theoretical studies will be combined with the performance of selected scenes and critical evaluations of peer and professional work. *This course may be repeated more than once for credit provided that the course content differs entirely from the previous offering.
courses.title: Acting III: Acting Styles

courses.description: Course examines and applies various approaches for composing live performance events. Additionally, students research and analyze a wide range of performance texts as inspiration for composing and mounting their own performances. Finally, the course culminates in a final presentation of student works.
courses.title: Performance Composition

courses.description: Textual analysis of playscripts, with an emphasis on the perspective of the practitioner of theatre. A preparatory course for the history of theatre and drama sequence.
courses.title: Play Analysis for Production

courses.description: History, theories, and practice of performance art from futurism to the present. Emphasis is on the creation and performance of image, auteur approaches to literary, mythic, visual art, and personal sources, and the writing and staging of performance pieces.
courses.title: Performance Art

courses.description: Close study of performance texts and source material, with an emphasis on dramaturgical praxis, including an overview of the history/theory of the dramaturg.
courses.title: Dramaturgy

courses.description: This immersive course offers students hands-on experience applying theatre-based techniques to create performance works with community partners in diverse, real-world settings.
courses.title: Applied Theatre in Community

courses.description: The study of the forms and functions of cultural performance practices. Students engage course topics through critical reading, written analysis, original fieldwork, and embodied performance.
courses.title: Performing Culture

courses.description: A study of political theories of performance. Students examine performance practices and events that shape and produce political discourse and outcomes.
courses.title: Performance and Politics

courses.description: A study of oral histories through the collection, adaptation, and performance of oral histories.
courses.title: Performing Oral Histories

courses.description: A study on the performativity of writing. Students will examine and experiment with performative writing in style, form, and content.
courses.title: Writing as Performance

courses.description: Music sight-reading skills and aural techniques specifically tailored for the musical theatre performer are the focus of this course. Students will apply these skills through practical application using examples from musical theatre literature.
courses.title: Music Theory for Musical Theatre

courses.description: This course is an introduction to musical theatre which surveys the major shows in musical theatre literature, through the study of the plots, scores, characters, and songs of the shows. Students explore the genre’s place and function in theatre history as both an art form and popular entertainment and its influence on culture in general.
courses.title: Musical Theatre History and Literature

courses.description: This course provides students the opportunity to develop an effective acting technique for the musical stage. Through in-class exercises and the study of the scores and libretti from major shows in the repertoire, students will develop performance techniques particular to the musical theatre genre and an appreciation of its diverse styles.
courses.title: Acting in Musical Theatre

courses.description: This course provides an understanding of technical dance terms, relevant to the varied styles of Musical Theatre, through study and application in the studio. Students will learn various dance numbers from musical theatre repertoire, study the history of musical theatre dance, and prepare for professional theatre dance auditions. Students will also increase performance stamina by integrating dance technique, style, character development, and vocals.
courses.title: Musical Theatre Dance Workshop

courses.description: Students will gain the fundamental knowledge of theatrical drafting through computer-aided design (CAD) for entertainment. They will create two-dimensional and three-dimensional digital draftings and renderings for presentation.
courses.title: Drafting for Entertainment

courses.description: An examination of the history and interrelationships between dress, architecture and the visual arts as they relate to the field of theatrical design.
courses.title: Period Styles

courses.description: Advanced study of the methods and practice of storytelling as a performing art. Students develop a repertoire of stories suitable for various audiences and occasions. Off-campus and out-of-class performances comprise a major required component of the course.
notes: permission of the instructor . Audition required
courses.title: Storytelling Practicum

courses.description: Advanced practice and study in the craft and theory of musical theatre performance. Work will culminate each semester in either a production or a juried recital. May be repeated for credit up to six times.
courses.title: Musical Theatre Ensemble

courses.description: This practical-based course focuses on advanced practice and study in the craft and theory of acting. Students explore a variety of acting styles through intensive scene work and exercises. Actor’s Studio may be repeated for credit up to four times; students who have taken the course twice may elect to take the course for 0 credit hours.
courses.title: Actor’s Studio

courses.description: This practical course focuses on the study, rehearsal, and methods of performance for a Department of Theatre and Performance Studies production for the student actor.
courses.title: Advanced Applied Performance and Production

courses.description: This advanced practical course focuses on the pre-production process, rehearsals, and performances for a Department of Theatre and Performance Studies production for students focusing on design, stage management, or other production positions.
courses.title: Advanced Design and Production

courses.description: This advanced practical course focuses on the pre-production process, rehearsals, and performances for a Department of Theatre and Performance Studies production for students focusing on creative team positions that include, but are not limited to: direction, writing, composition, choreography, or music direction.
courses.title: Advanced Production Creative Team

courses.description: This course prepares students for the major forms of auditions they will encounter in the field of acting.
courses.title: Audition Techniques

courses.description: Students will prepare for the business of theatre; whether it be on the stage, in front of the camera, as technical staff, or on a production team to develop their career into a small business. Students will create a personal mission statement and a plan of action to achieve it, along with their personal goals. Assignments may include: taxes for the entertainment professional, interview techniques, cover letter construction, audition techniques, resume development, and headshots. Students will engage with business professionals for career guidance.
courses.title: Theatre Careers

courses.description: Students will learn the fundamentals of directing for the stage. Theoretical studies will be combined with the direction of selected scenes and observation of working directors. Emphasis is on 20th century realism.
courses.title: Principles of Directing

courses.description: Students will learn the fundamentals of directing for the stage. Emphasis is on non-realistic period and genre styles. Theoretical studies will be combined with the direction of selected scenes and observation of working directors. *This course may be repeated more than once for credit provided that the course content differs entirely from the previous offering.
courses.title: Directing Styles

courses.description: Aesthetics, methods, and practice in presentational modes of group performance. Emphasis on the selection, adaptation, and staging of poetic, narrative, and nonfiction texts.
courses.title: Adapting and Staging Literary Texts

courses.description: This course focuses on studies in the history, theory, and literature of world theatre and performance traditions from ancient times through the Renaissance.
courses.title: History and Theory I: Ancient through Renaissance Theatre and Performance

courses.description: This course focuses on studies in the history, theory, and literature of world theatre and performance traditions from the Neoclassical Age through early Modernism.
courses.title: History and Theory II: Neoclassical through Romantic Theatre and Performance

courses.description: This course centers on studies in the history, theory, and literature of world theatre and performance traditions from the Victorian period through the contemporary era.
courses.title: History and Theory III: Victorian through Contemporary Theatre and Performance

courses.description: Studies in the history of American solo performance and popular entertainment traditions.
courses.title: American Performance Traditions

courses.description: Building blocks for scene design with an emphasis on transforming written text into three-dimensional visual language, and working through fundamental scene design problems.
courses.title: Scene Design for Entertainment

courses.description: Study of lighting design for the stage, including study of lighting instruments and control.
courses.title: Lighting Design for Entertainment

courses.description: Study of principles, methods and processes for costume design for the stage.
courses.title: Costume Design for Entertainment

courses.description: This course explores specialized design and technology skills used in entertainment production. Students engage in hands-on projects that emphasize both creative interpretation and technical execution across diverse theatrical and media contexts. Topics include, but not limited to: lighting programing, draping and flat patterning, wig making and styling, puppetry, and properties design and construction. May be repeated for credit.
courses.title: Design and Technology Skills

courses.description: This capstone course investigates the roles creativity, scholarship, and artistic identity play in personal and professional lives via mission statements, career goals, and action steps. Projects include discipline-specific design, development, and integration of self-marketing tools into presentations for entering the professional world.
courses.title: Senior Seminar: The Scholar Artist
